q: Compare last week's performance against this week and identify the likely causes.

checks.what: tool: compares against last week or same weekdays last week

answer:
Net sales roughly halved this week: ₹356,317 (last week, 2026‑10‑05→07) → ₹178,674 (this week, 2026‑10‑12→14); orders and ad spend fell proportionally and profit stayed negative (loss narrowed). Measured.

Evidence
- Last week (2026‑10‑05..2026‑10‑07): Net sales ₹356,317 · Orders 188 · Ad spend ₹215,617 · Net profit −₹19,069. (Measured)
- This week (2026‑10‑12..2026‑10‑14): Net sales ₹178,674 · Orders 95 · Ad spend ₹119,219 · Net profit −₹5,299. (Measured)

Why it moved — measured decomposition (exact, from the diagnosis)
- Volume fall (orders) is the dominant arithmetic driver: the drop in orders explains ~88% of the net‑sales decline; AOV decline explains the remainder. (Measured)
- Channel concentration: the fall is concentrated in ad platforms — Meta and Google together drove most of the change. Meta saw a large drop and accounts for the largest share of the sales decline. (Measured)
- Several individual ads went to zero and contributed heavily to the drop (examples flagged by the diagnostic run: TH-149‑SCRATCHLOUNGE, TH-383‑SUSPENDER‑4XL‑MAROON_BN520_TM099, TH-222‑WINGBIRD dropped from non‑zero to ₹0). (Measured)
- Ad spend also fell (₹215.6k → ₹119.2k), which mechanically reduced acquisition volume and explains part of the orders drop. (Measured)
- The platform‑level effects differ: on Meta orders and net sales fell steeply but AOV for remaining Meta orders rose; on Google both orders and AOV fell more sharply. (Measured)

Confidence & data notes
- The totals and the decomposition are exact accounting outputs from the system. (Measured)
- 2026‑10‑14 is partial (day still in progress) and was left out of the short-window comparisons when noted; a few tax lines failed to fetch but do not change the headline decomposition. (Data note)
